method: Literal authored fixture, positive/negative transformations and rejection diagnostics from the pre-existing source-index contract. Expected outcomes are not generated from a proposed optimization. The existing typed comparator and canonical guard are both checked on the same finite canonical reference domain.
reference_precondition: Finite canonical catalogue-owned rows, excluding float-bearing reports. Neither the fixture nor this test grants source authority.
source_fixture_scope: Most adversarial variants use a tiny authored SearchIndex replacement only at the reconstruction boundary, with a call/failure sentinel. One separate test uses the real installed SearchIndex and the already-frozen retrieval report. Existing 19 operator-context/source tests remain unchanged and are still required.
decimal_limit_scope: For the document matrix only, the test temporarily sets Python integer string conversion to the declared 640-digit limit and restores it in finally; the oversized integer is 10**1000. It does not change production configuration.
independence_limits: Exposed engineering regression, not a blind linguistic evaluation.
Use of existing _same_json in direct assertions is the subject under test, not an oracle recurrence. Literal outcomes are pinned separately.
Canonical catalogue checking establishes the fixture reference domain; it does not generate the expected accept/reject list.
No production edit, new representation, new comparator, CI relaxation or source-license claim.
